**Review of the Assam Breakfast product page draft**

**Claims list**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "malty, full-bodied black tea" | Product/flavour fact, fine as written |
| "stands up to milk" | Taste description, fine |
| "boosts your immunity through winter" | **Unsupported.** Health claim, not on the allowlist, no source. |
| "Certified organic by the Soil Association" | Allowlisted |
| "100g tin" | Product fact (size), fine |
| "makes around 40 cups" | Brewing/size fact, fine as written under product facts |

**Problems**

1. **"boosts your immunity through winter"** is a health claim. Tea can't be claimed to boost immunity: it isn't on the allowlist, there's no source, and in the UK, unauthorised health claims on food and drink break the nutrition and health claims rules (and would likely be flagged by ad platforms if reused). Remove it. Replace it with a sensory or occasion line, for example: "A malty, full-bodied black tea that stands up to milk. Good for dark winter mornings."

**Slop/structure check:** No ban-list words, no exclamation marks, no rhetorical openers. The opening fragment "Assam Breakfast." is the product name, which is fine.

**Suggested compliant version**

> Assam Breakfast. A malty, full-bodied black tea that stands up to milk. Certified organic by the Soil Association. 100g tin, makes around 40 cups.

Not ready to publish as written. Cut the immunity claim first.
